items.prompt: Given \(f(x)=x^2-7x+10\): (a) factorise \(f(x)\); (b) solve \(f(x)=0\); (c) solve \(f(x)<0\), justifying the interval.
A jacket is £120. (a) Its price rises by \(15\%\). Calculate the new price. (b) This new price falls by \(20\%\). Find the final price. (c) Explain why the original price is not restored.

Two similar triangles have corresponding sides \(4\text{ cm}\) and \(10\text{ cm}\). The smaller area is \(12\text{ cm}^2\). (a) Find the length scale factor. (b) Find the larger area. (c) Explain the relationship between length scale and area scale.
Let \(f(x)=3x-7\), \(g(x)=x^2+2\). (a) Find \(f(g(x))\). (b) Find \(g(f(x))\). (c) Determine \(f^{-1}(x)\) and verify a composition.

A cuboid measures \(3\text{ cm}\) by \(4\text{ cm}\) by \(12\text{ cm}\). (a) Find its space diagonal. (b) Unfold the two side faces measuring \(3\times12\) and \(4\times12\) cm; find the shortest route between opposite vertices along these two faces. (c) Compare the two routes.
The height of a ball is \(h(t)=-5t^2+20t+1\), where \(t\ge0\). (a) Complete the square. (b) Find the maximum height and time. (c) Explain why the model must stop applying at some future time.
(a) Simplify \(3\sqrt{12}-\sqrt{27}\). (b) Rationalise \(\frac5{\sqrt5-1}\). (c) Explain why the conjugate removes the irrational denominator.
Let \(f(x)=\frac{x^2-9}{x^2-3x}\). (a) Simplify \(f(x)\). (b) State all excluded inputs from the original fraction. (c) Solve \(f(x)=2\), checking restrictions.
The line \(y=x+1\) intersects \(x^2+y^2=13\). (a) Eliminate \(y\). (b) Find both intersection points. (c) Verify one solution in the two original equations.
Let \(f(x)=2x+1\), \(g(x)=x^2-2\). (a) Find \(f(g(x))\). (b) Find \(g(f(x))\). (c) Solve \(f(g(x))=7\) for all real \(x\).
In triangle \(ABC\), \(\angle A=30^\circ\), \(\angle B=60^\circ\) and \(a=8\text{ cm}\), opposite \(A\). (a) Find angle \(C\). (b) Find side \(b\) exactly. (c) Calculate the area exactly.

Let \(\vec{OA}=\mathbf a\), \(\vec{OB}=\mathbf b\). Point \(M\) is the midpoint of \(AB\). Point \(N\) lies on \(OA\) with \(\vec{ON}=\frac13\mathbf a\). Express (a) \(\vec{OM}\), (b) \(\vec{NM}\), (c) \(\vec{BM}\) in terms of \(\mathbf a,\mathbf b\).
